title: Navigation API: Perform navigation & Update URL and history (via replaceState/pushState) race?

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[Perform a navigation API traversal step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#performing-a-navigation-api-traversal) appends steps to run on the session history queue, step 12 and its substeps. This is to run in parallel on the session history queue.

[Shared history push/replace-state steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#shared-history-push/replace-state-steps) eventually runs on the event loop, and as a last step calls [URL and history update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#url-and-history-update-steps)

In step 11 of [URL and history update steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#url-and-history-update-steps) we mutate stuff inside [Update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation).

This mutation is not happening on the session history queue. Step 13 appends to the session history queue to run [Finalize a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#finalize-a-same-document-navigation).

But given that 11 runs on the event loop, a set of appended steps from [Perform a navigation API traversal step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#performing-a-navigation-api-traversal) can be running, and worse, it can have already run past step 12.3 before step 11 has completed on the event loop. That means that the check it performed, is no longer true.

So the spec shall hit an assertion because of this, because deep in the callstack of [Perform a navigation API traversal step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#performing-a-navigation-api-traversal) we end up in [update the navigation API entries for a same-document navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation) - specifically [the branch for when navigation type is "traverse"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-a-same-document-navigation:~:text=navigation%2E-,Assert%3A%20navigation%27s%20current%20entry%20index%20is%20not%20%E2%88%921).

Hitting that exact assertion in the Gecko implementation is what led me to this finding and as far as I can tell, I don't think we are "saved" by anything along the way in these algorithms.

@noamr || @farre
